inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,065 normalized lines, including the abstract, historical and analytic setup, Kadiri iteration, all four error-term components, simulated-annealing construction, coefficient and result tables, limitations, applications, acknowledgements, and references. The prose makes the main mechanisms recoverable; several displayed formulas and coefficient tables retain text-layer layout risk and should be checked against the retained PDF before exact reuse.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the improved classical zero-free region and attributes it to polynomial search plus sharper error analysis.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Contrasts classical and Korobov-Vinogradov regions, defines the admissible trigonometric-polynomial extremal problem, and states the two main results.

sections_inspected.label: Kadiri's method
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds a contradiction framework around a hypothetical zero, transfers polynomial data to an explicit bound on R0, and iterates the bound.

sections_inspected.label: Improvements
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces the new polynomial, retains sign information in the error term, balances two denominator bounds, and quantifies the improvement sources.

sections_inspected.label: Analyzing the error term
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Decomposes C(eta), sharpens exponential and zero-tail estimates, and turns remaining integrals into rigorously bounded numerical pieces.

sections_inspected.label: Searching for trigonometric polynomials
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the annealing surrogate, square-modulus parametrization, feasibility tests, incremental updates, and search schedule.

sections_inspected.label: Results and potential improvements
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Certifies improved Landau and zero-free constants, diagnoses surrogate mismatch, and estimates the method's finite-height ceiling.

sections_inspected.label: Applications
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Propagates the zero-free region to explicit prime-number-theorem error bounds and related Chebyshev-function estimates.

sections_inspected.label: Acknowledgements and references
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Provides computational acknowledgements and bibliographic provenance; no additional source argument occurs here.

accepted_units.title: Finite-height role of classical zero-free regions
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes an asymptotically stronger region from a classical region that remains quantitatively competitive at finite height, motivating optimization of the classical constant rather than treating asymptotics as the sole criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 76-83 reiterate the finite-height comparison and historical improvement of R0.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The two region formulas are legible in the extraction, but exact exponents and constants should be verified against the PDF for formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Admissible nonnegative trigonometric polynomials as the common certificate family
accepted_units.why_material: It identifies the recurring structural constraints—global nonnegativity, nonnegative coefficients, and a1>a0—and shows that improving the zero-free constant has repeatedly depended on choosing a better certificate in this family.
accepted_units.context_note: The historical table at lines 63-73 supplies the associated constants and parameterized degree-four family.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The factorized polynomial and coefficient conditions are recoverable from text; no figure is needed.

accepted_units.title: Landau's extremal functional bridges polynomial design to R0
accepted_units.why_material: The unit defines Pn, Vn, and its limiting value V, then records how bounds on this polynomial extremum transfer to permissible classical zero-free constants, including Stechkin's sharpening.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the source's first explicit compression of an analytic number-theory goal into a polynomial optimization problem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula layout is mildly degraded; the square-root denominator and Stechkin factor require PDF verification before exact transcription.

accepted_units.title: Two-lever improvement program: better certificates and retained error information
accepted_units.why_material: The authors frame their advance as the combination of randomized search for higher-degree certificates and a sharper use of the analytic error term, a reusable decomposition between representation search and proof-bound refinement.
accepted_units.context_note: The resulting polynomial and error analysis are developed in Sections 3-6.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded; Table 2 only supplies an earlier numerical example.

accepted_units.title: Improved zero-free and Landau bounds
accepted_units.why_material: The source states both its explicit zero-free theorem and the improved upper bound on the limiting polynomial extremum, connecting the analytic and optimization outputs while keeping them distinct.
accepted_units.context_note: The finite interval in which the classical result is best is reported at lines 152-153.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact inequalities and powers are formula-dependent and should be checked against the PDF; the surrounding prose fixes their intended roles.

accepted_units.title: Bootstrap a known zero-free region against a hypothetical boundary zero
accepted_units.why_material: Kadiri's method starts from an established constant R and a target lower parameter r, assumes a zero in the intervening strip, and seeks an intermediate R0 that rules it out; this exposes the logical bootstrap underlying the numerical iteration.
accepted_units.context_note: Subsequent definitions normalize the hypothetical zero's height and feed the final inequality.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The inequalities are readable, with ordinary displayed-formula dependence.

accepted_units.title: Kernel monotonicity removes the unknown zero height from the R0 bound
accepted_units.why_material: After defining normalized height variables, a compactly supported kernel, and admissible kappa/delta constraints, the method derives an R0 inequality and uses monotonicity of K and sign monotonicity of C to replace the unknown w and eta by endpoint data.
accepted_units.context_note: The many auxiliary formulas are setup for the conceptual endpoint reduction at lines 260-274.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strong formula dependence with text-layer fraction and derivative-layout risk; retain the semantic unit but verify every exact definition from the PDF before training or formal use.

accepted_units.title: Nested replacement iteration converts a local improvement into a stable constant
accepted_units.why_material: The algorithm repeatedly replaces the assumed region constant with the newly certified one while keeping r below it, uses inner and outer tolerances, and stops only when the improvement stabilizes, making the bootstrap computationally explicit.
accepted_units.context_note: This records certification logic rather than merely the final decimal.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose and decimal parameters are clear; exact reported values should remain source-linked.

accepted_units.title: Split the eta range and balance complementary denominator bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Introducing eta1 preserves useful negativity from C(eta): small eta uses a stronger lower bound on w, while larger eta retains -C(eta1). A minimax choice balances the two, and the source attributes most of the final gain to this retention plus the new polynomial.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 325-336 give the binary search and nested stopping rules; lines 337-340 separate the polynomial/error gain from the increased verified height.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (3.1) is layout-sensitive, but the two-range balancing argument is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: C1 and C2: sharpen a reusable exponential majorant with directed rounding
accepted_units.why_material: The error is decomposed into four terms; for C2, precomputed moments replace repeated integration and a cubic exponential majorant sharpens the estimate, while direction-aware rounding preserves rigor.
accepted_units.context_note: The detailed C1 coefficients are supporting setup; the reusable mechanism is moment precomputation plus a valid polynomial majorant and outward rounding.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Dense extracted formulas are vulnerable to fraction and prime-mark corruption; prose at lines 408-429 reliably states the computational mechanism.

accepted_units.title: C3: replace a global zero-counting error bound by an explicit tail sum
accepted_units.why_material: Instead of inheriting an explicit N(T) error estimate, the authors express the needed contribution as a tail over zeta zeros, subtract a computable initial segment at t=0, and use Lehman's monotone-sum integral bound for positive t.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a method change, not only a tighter constant: known discrete data and an analytic tail bound are combined at a chosen cutoff.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The tail-sum and integral formulas are central and extraction-sensitive; exact constants and denominators need PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: C4: isolate numerically tractable middle ranges and analytically bound tails
accepted_units.why_material: A piecewise majorant for U0 and symmetry reduce the integral; the domain is split at formula-change points and around its moving peak, middle pieces are evaluated numerically, and logarithmic tail inequalities yield explicit analytic bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: The chosen epsilon completes a hybrid analytic-numerical upper bound rather than an uncontrolled quadrature.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very strong formula and reading-order dependence; the prose preserves the partition strategy, but the displayed final bound requires original-PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Use a cheap Landau surrogate inside simulated annealing
accepted_units.why_material: The source explains why the true Kadiri objective is too expensive for repeated search and substitutes the fast Landau functional, while retaining annealing's controlled willingness to cross local barriers.
accepted_units.context_note: Later results show that this surrogate is useful but imperfect, so this unit should be linked to units u017 and u018.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The acceptance probability and surrogate formula are clear, with minor displayed-formula dependence.

accepted_units.title: Square-modulus coordinates make global nonnegativity automatic
accepted_units.why_material: Parametrizing f as the squared magnitude of a complex polynomial converts a global nonnegativity constraint into an invariant of the representation; feasibility then reduces to coefficient autocorrelations, nonnegativity checks, and a1>a0.
accepted_units.context_note: The authors note this is also computationally efficient because autocorrelations can be maintained directly.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The square-modulus and autocorrelation formulas are essential but legible; verify summation indices from the PDF before implementation.

accepted_units.title: Incremental autocorrelation updates keep annealing inside the admissible set
accepted_units.why_material: A one-coordinate move updates all affected autocorrelations in linear time, rejects infeasible states, applies the annealing rule to valid states, then combines cooling, greedy descent, shrinking step size, and diversified parallel runs.
accepted_units.context_note: The coefficient figure at lines 722-732 interrupts the prose but is not needed to understand the algorithm; lines 737-745 resume the schedule.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The update-index text is compact and should be verified before coding; the algorithmic roles are prose-recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Refined annealing yields the degree-40 Landau certificate
accepted_units.why_material: Coarse searches followed by finer local passes produce F40 and a strictly improved upper bound for V40, illustrating how heuristic exploration becomes a checkable certificate once a concrete admissible polynomial is fixed.
accepted_units.context_note: Figures 1-3 and Table 4 hold the coefficient-level evidence and comparative values.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The bound is prose-readable; independent reuse requires exact coefficient verification from the retained PDF or original numerical artifact.

accepted_units.title: A good Landau polynomial need not optimize the true zero-free constant
accepted_units.why_material: Applying Kadiri's calculation to record Landau polynomials reveals that their ranking for V does not determine their ranking for R0, explicitly diagnosing surrogate-objective mismatch.
accepted_units.context_note: This motivates rescoring the broader candidate pool with the expensive target objective.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded; Table 4 supplies numerical instances.

accepted_units.title: Rescore near-optimal surrogate candidates under the true objective
accepted_units.why_material: The authors test hundreds of thousands of strong Landau candidates with Kadiri's objective, find many better R0 certificates, and refine the best degree-16 candidate; the eventual winner is not the degree-16 Landau record.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a concrete two-stage search pattern: cheap broad surrogate exploration followed by expensive target-aligned selection and local refinement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded; Table 5 is needed only to reconstruct the final certificate exactly.

accepted_units.title: Increasing verified RH height has a diminishing asymptotic payoff in this method
accepted_units.why_material: Holding the polynomial and other choices fixed while varying T0 yields an empirical formula approaching a limiting R0, which identifies finite verified height as a lever with bounded long-run benefit rather than an unlimited route to improvement.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 836-840 pose the sensitivity question; lines 895-946 supply the computation and inferred ceiling.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The fitted expression and very large powers are formula-dependent and should be checked against the PDF; the limiting interpretation is stated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Zero-free width propagates to explicit prime-counting error bounds
accepted_units.why_material: The improved zero-free region is converted into sharper explicit bounds for theta, psi, and pi-li; the source also notes that a shifted-log zero-free form is asymptotically equivalent yet could further improve the finite explicit corollaries.
accepted_units.context_note: The proofs largely invoke prior transfer arguments, so the useful unit is the dependency pattern and stated consequences rather than repeated details.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several displayed bounds contain radicals and exponents with extraction risk; exact statements require PDF verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Certificate search plus analytic transfer
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source separates globally valid certificate construction from the analytic map that scores a certificate for a zero-free region, and shows why a cheap extremal surrogate must be followed by target-aligned rescoring.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This mechanism is demonstrated for this admissible polynomial family and Kadiri's fixed framework; it does not establish that the same surrogate-transfer pattern works for other zero-free methods.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Rigor-preserving hybrid computation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Heuristic search contributes candidate objects, while proof-valid numerics arise only after monotone majorants, explicit tails, interval partitions, outward rounding, and source-linked certificate data turn computations into one-sided bounds.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The normalized text does not itself provide machine-checkable interval logs or exact arithmetic artifacts, so exact certification must be recovered from the original source or associated computation.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Diagnosing the remaining improvement frontier
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Most realized gain comes from jointly improving the certificate and error use; surrogate mismatch can be repaired by rescoring, whereas increasing verified height alone appears to approach a finite ceiling inside the method.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The ceiling is an empirical fit under fixed choices and is not a general impossibility result for all parameter changes or zero-free-region techniques.

within_source_saturation: The full source is saturated at the mechanism level: retained units cover motivation, definitions, analytic transfer, iterative certification, every distinct error-control idea, representation and search design, numerical certificate selection, surrogate failure and repair, sensitivity limits, and downstream applications. Further units would predominantly isolate coefficient lists, routine formula expansion, repeated parameter tables, or bibliography rather than add a distinct reusable mathematical move.
